vulnerabilities.description: MCPToolCallView trusts the client-supplied X-Gateway-Roles header for policy-engine role scoping. Its permission class (IsAuthenticatedOrGatewayInternal, mcp_connector/views.py:119) allows any JWT-authenticated user to call the endpoint directly (not just the trusted gateway), so a user can forge this header to bypass role-scoped MCP tool policies.

UserCreateSerializer.create() calls User.objects.create_user() directly, bypassing Django's validate_password() / AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS (common-password, complexity, numeric-only checks). Only min_length=12 is enforced for admin-created accounts.

GatewayAPIKey post_delete handler deletes the Redis key synchronously instead of via transaction.on_commit (unlike the KillSwitch/ModelState handlers in the same file). A rolled-back delete transaction leaves Redis and Postgres in disagreement over the key's existence, causing gateway auth state desync.

PolicyTestView validates policy_id with enabled=True (line 981) but re-queries it via Policy.objects.filter(pk=policy_id) without that filter (line 1005); the lazy queryset is evaluated later, so a policy disabled in that window is still applied (TOCTOU).

REST_FRAMEWORK DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES is AllowAny project-wide; every view checked in this scan explicitly overrides it, but this is a fail-open default that will silently expose any future view whose author forgets to set permission_classes.

Dependency/package-version audit was not performed — pyproject.toml lives outside this session's permitted directory (control/ai_mesh_control) and was not read. Re-run with access to control/pyproject.toml and frontend/package.json for a real CVE/version check.

recommendations: Change MCPToolCallView's permission model so X-Gateway-Roles is only honored on requests authenticated as the trusted gateway (IsGatewayInternalOnly), not on direct end-user JWT calls; for JWT calls, derive roles server-side from the authenticated user's own role assignments.
Call Django's validate_password(password, user) inside UserCreateSerializer.create() (and any other admin-provisioning path) so the full AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS chain applies, not just min_length.
Wrap the GatewayAPIKey post_delete Redis removal in transaction.on_commit to match the KillSwitch/ModelState handlers and eliminate the rollback-desync window.

In PolicyTestView, either re-fetch policies_qs with the same enabled=True/organization=org filter used for the initial validation, or force evaluation of policy_row itself instead of a separately-filtered queryset.
Set an explicit restrictive DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES (e.g. IsAuthenticated) and treat AllowAny as an intentional per-view opt-in, to remove the fail-open default.
Run a dependency audit (pip-audit / npm audit) against control/pyproject.toml and frontend/package.json — not covered in this pass due to directory sandboxing.
